trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +407.94% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +354.91pp residual after beta, -38.6% max drawdown, 0.31% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +407.94% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +393.53pp.
The beta premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+58.00% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The market premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+15.79% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +407.94% total, about +53.03pp is explained by carrying beta 3.68 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.42); the residual +354.91pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
CVNA contributed +169,291 USD (41% of net P&L) across 18 closed trades; META was the biggest drag at -26,293 USD.
Execution cost 312 USD (0.31% of starting capital, 1.6 bp per fill, 1.6 bp of the 1,997,336 USD traded). 73% of that was spread/depth/impact and 27% was explicit fees and rebates.
57 closed round trips, 87.7% winners, profit factor 12.86, average winner +8,823 vs average loser -4,902 USD, median holding 105 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 6915 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: META long 2025-09-17 to 2026-09-16, -25,888 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -38.61% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-03-06, recovered 2026-04-08. Average gross exposure 379% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.24x.
Daily returns were +0.33 skewed with excess kurtosis +0.62; historical 95% VaR -6.63%/day with CVaR -8.58%/day. Worst single session -10.64%, best +17.41%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.

Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Volatility decay: repeated rebalancing to a fixed leverage in a choppy market bleeds value; A 2x gross book in a 10% market drawdown is a 20% account drawdown with no brake.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): Beta is estimated on trailing data, so the basket chases whatever was volatile last quarter.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 127.0pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @BetaChaser_3xProxy (Beta Chaser) ran the "levered beta" archetype. Declared thesis: In a rising market the highest-beta names deliver the highest return. This participant is the human equivalent of a 3x levered ETF: hold the top-beta basket at maximum permitted leverage and rebalance weekly. Entry: Rank the universe by realised beta to the S&P 500 over 63 sessions; Hold the top 5 beta names equally weighted at 2.0x gross; Re-rank weekly. Exit: Only at the weekly rebalance; never de-risks on a drawdown. Sizing: 40% of equity per name = 200% gross. Leverage: 2.0x gross, always invested. Cadence: weekly, horizon all season. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Maximum market exposure at all times: if the market goes up, this participant should win.
